_: PERMDESIGN-1. The ONE source of the narrow Bash allow and deny rules `tools/apply-allow-rules.sh` merges into each repository's Claude Code settings. `{path}` becomes the plugin's installed path (absolute, `~/`, and the skills link), never a path relative to the session's working tree, which the session can edit. `target` is relative to the plugin, or to the repository itself with `"base": "repo"`; a rule whose target does not exist there is not written. Narrow rules only: auto mode drops a broad interpreter rule such as `Bash(python*)`, and keeps a rule that names one script and one subcommand.

allow.why: land a branch: main read and fast-forwarded in one command, refused when main moved
change a live limit (owner keys still need --owner, which is denied)
the safe close: ledger, screen, host and attended checks decide
close finished sessions while memory is over the line
close every finished session; never `close:*`, which would allow `--replay --out <any file>`
run a script whose exact bytes are in the reviewed ledger; anything else is refused

deny.why: the owner's switches are set from the owner's own terminal
